status: preregistered before the full audit; development checks used one round for timing/coverage only (no optimality numbers were read)
request: Owner 2026-11-08: take the cloud human games, cut them to the endgame and check whether the model can always play the optimal solution there; with one seat under its control, can it beat the opponents, and when the side that actually lost had a better line, can it find it. Going out first is not the only goal: avoiding a double-down (-3 -> -2) also counts.
kind: Diagnostic audit only. No training, no gradient update, no change to the web champion, menu, or any run. Human records are evaluation data here, not training data.

data.source: Cloud D1 guandan-human-games-v1, kind=game, read-only query with the owner's local wrangler OAuth (export token not present on this Mac). Saved under the ignored ai/shared/data/human-games/d1-snapshot-20261108/; records are not committed.
data.composition: All 26 rounds: 4 human seats (humanMask 15), Clint site appVersion c1977…, no bot or timeout actions, 2,210 human actions; all replay legally with web/src/collection/validate.mjs.
data.trust: unverified_browser (legal replay is not identity verification).
data.assisted: Match 5f687c12 has 678 actions flagged assisted=true; the data README records the owner's confirmation that these flags came from testing the evaluation UI. They are kept (--keep-assisted=5f687c12) and every human-rate result is also reported for unassisted actions only.

student.note: Endgame oracle-guiding student (section 57); trained only for tables with <= 32 cards, so its rates are reported for <= 32 cards.

models.policy: Greedy argmax on own hand + public history (policyState), finishing move and single candidate automatic; no web balanced style, no endgame proof shortcut.

solver.definition: Exact perfect-information team minimax over the signed single-round result (+-1/+-2/+-3 for the mover's team) with the same candidate generator as play; values are exact, not proxies (no tempo/control/bomb terms).
solver.check: createSolver equals solveEndgame on values and every root move for 30 random endgames (new test).

design.tail: Walk each round back from its last action, solving every position, and stop at the first one with > 40 cards on the table or over budget. The audited tail depends only on solver tractability, not on the moves; it includes early double-up endings with many cards left.
design.decisionAudit: Every human decision in the tail. Best value vs value after the human's move, the champion's choice and the student's choice. 'choice' = not automatic and >= 2 candidates; 'critical' = a choice where some candidate loses value (optimalMoves < candidates). Optimal = keeps the exact value; regret = best - chosen.
design.afterHumanError: Critical decisions where the human's move lost value: did the model choose a value-keeping move in that same position?
design.takeover: From the first tail position: a model controls one active seat (each seat separately) or both seats of a team; every other seat plays the first solver-optimal candidate with all hands visible. Success = final signed points equal the start position's exact value (the maximum possible against perfect opponents). Subsets: teams whose real result was below the exact value; real loss but exact win; real double-down (-3) but exact better than -3.

metrics: Optimal rates with round-cluster bootstrap 95% intervals (2,000 draws, seed 20261108), mean regret in round points; takeover success rates with the same interval, mean shortfall, outcome transitions actual->exact->achieved. No acceptance threshold: this is descriptive.
limits: Only 26 rounds from 2 matches of the same four players on one site; intervals are conditional on these rounds and cannot be generalised to all human play.
Perfect-information optimum is an upper bound: a player who sees only their own hand cannot always reach it (strategy fusion). A miss is not necessarily a mistake given the information available.
Single-round signed points only; whole-match effects (pass A, aFail) are not scored.
Opponents in takeover are perfect-information solvers, stronger than any real opponent.
outputs: Per-decision rows stay in the ignored workspace (no cards). Committed: run.json and summary.json (counts and values only).
followUp: Any training on human endgames needs its own preregistration; 26 rounds are too few to train on directly.
